attempts.summary: Configured daily log rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 via /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app (daily, rotate 7, compress, delaycompress, copytruncate) so the app can keep writing to the same inode after rotation. Validated syntax with `logrotate -d`, then forced two real rotations to prove: (1) copytruncate preserves the file's inode so a writer never loses its file handle, (2) compressed rotations accumulate correctly (.1 -> .2.gz) with delaycompress deferring compression by one cycle, consistent with a 7-rotation retention policy. Reset the log directory to a clean baseline afterward. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, issued `systemctl reboot` via a backgrounded ack-then-disconnect wrapper, polled through the outage, confirmed boot_id changed (636556ce... -> 3e7264d8...) and uptime-since reset to 08:26:09, then verified post-reboot that the logrotate config file, the log file/content, and the logrotate.timer (active+enabled, next run scheduled) all recovered intact.
